senses.gloss: (denom. of קוֹרָה, q. v.) to lay beams; to cover.
(denom. of קִיר I, q. v.) to wall up, close.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 10b:23">Ber. 10ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="II Kings 4:10">II Kings IV, 10</cite>) <he>עלייה … וקֵירוּהָ</he> it was an open upper room (a balcony), and they closed it up.
<cite ref="Mishnah Moed Katan 1:4">M. Kat. I, 4</cite> <he>מְקָרִין את הפירצה וכ׳</he> you may close up a breach during the festive week.
<cite ref="Moed Katan 7a:4">Ib. 7ᵃ</cite> <he>כיצד מקרין וכ׳</he> in what way is it to be done?… With shrubbery or bay-trees.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sukkah 1:8">Succ. I, 8</cite> <he>המְקָרֶה סוכתו וכ׳</he> he who covers his Succah with spits or boards of a bed-side.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 1:7">Lev. R. s. 1</cite> <he>היה מקרה בקורות וכ׳</he> he covered the building with joists, and wrote the name of the king on them; a. e.—Part. pass. <he>מְקוֹרֶה</he>; f. <cite ref="M02401"><he>מְקוֹרָה</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 1:1:2">Y. Succ. I, 51ᵈ</cite> top <he>סוכה מ׳ פסולה</he> a Succah covered with beams is ritually unfit; <he>מבוי מ׳ כשר</he> a covered alley is fit (for Sabbath movements).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nazir 9:3:6">Y. Naz. IX, 57ᵈ</cite> <he>מערה מ׳</he> a vaulted cave.
